about.purpose: Machine-readable index of this GitHub account. Written for AI assistants (any vendor) and for people arriving cold, so neither has to infer the layout from repo names.
about.subject: Flat-to-VR game modding: converting existing flat PC games to VR, plus the reusable knowledge produced along the way.
about.stated_goal: The playable VR mods matter, but the durable goal is the knowledge, published so others can reuse it.
about.layout_change: 2026-08-30: consolidated from six repos per game (101 repos) to ONE public repo per game plus one private staging monorepo (22 repos). Each former repo is now a folder inside its game repo, with full git history preserved behind a subtree join commit.

headline: 2026-09-14: two cameras found in one day. Dead Space 2's projection is at constant register c4 and Prototype's at c0, both left-handed, both read live through a d3d9 proxy built, self-tested and deployed the same day. Six of the eight projects started on 2026-09-13 were advanced; four of them by static reading alone. The day also produced two corrections to this file's own earlier claims and one account-wide latent bug found in three other projects' proxies.

read_first.if: You are about to drive or automate one of these games
read_first.why: Keys, menu routes, state detection and entry points, per game. Vendor-neutral. Its UNIVERSAL.md carries the method rules that prevent the most wasted work.

read_first.if: You are doing reverse-engineering or VR conversion work
read_first.why: The engine-agnostic PLAYBOOK, the tool catalogue, and tools/ (small utilities that already earned their place).

read_first.if: You want what is known about an engine family
read_first.why: Cross-engine library. docs/engines/ has one page per engine family.

read_first.if: You are resuming work on a specific game
read_first.read: that game repo's engine-research/ENGINE-DOSSIER.md, then its modding-notes/ folder
read_first.why: The dossier is distilled current truth for that engine, including dead ends. The notes are the chronological ledger.

mod/.holds: release packaging and player-facing docs; the releases themselves are GitHub Releases on the game repo
mod/.note: Often sparse. A project with no release yet has a near-empty mod/; this is expected, not a mistake.

dev-archive/.holds: the live working mod source AND the messy dev history: snapshots, probes, recon evidence, dead ends
dev-archive/.note: This is where the actual mod source lives, commonly under dev-archive/tools/.

modding-notes/.holds: readable field notes and the dated progress ledger

engine-research/.holds: ENGINE-DOSSIER.md — distilled truth about that game's engine, including a dead-ends section

external-research/.holds: leads gathered from public sources by a research-only session; INDEX.md plus topics/

staging.holds: unverified work-in-progress for every project, one folder per game (staging/<prefix>/); the cross-machine handoff channel

conventions.history_note: Each folder was its own repo until 2026-08-30. Full per-file history is preserved and reachable through the folder's subtree join commit (git log the merge parents). The old <prefix>-<suffix> repo names redirect only where a repo was renamed (each game's -mod became the game repo).

session_lanes.note: Five kinds of session, each typed as a slash-command. They are designed to run at the same time; one_writer_per_file below is what keeps them from colliding.

lanes./lm (live modding): the only lane that may launch a game, attach a debugger or drive VR
lanes./pd (parallel development): advances every project as far as it can with no game running
lanes./gr (game research): public-research sweep; curates each game repo external-research/
lanes./gs (github sweep): read-only hygiene audit of the whole estate; curates nothing

background_agents.never_in_includes: the standing /gate-watch background watcher, which is otherwise permitted everywhere (owner ruling, 2026-09-03): those two lanes run fully inline.
background_agents.rationale: The three sweep lanes are breadth-first over many projects and leave their output as reviewable commits. /lm drives a live game, which no agent may do. /gs is an audit whose value is that the session performed each check itself, so a second-hand summary would defeat it.
background_agents.still_applies: Even where allowed, agents must be few and each must have a job the owner could name without asking; ad-hoc fan-out is not the intent.

one_writer_per_file.rule: Every file has exactly one kind of session that may edit it. Reading is unrestricted.

lanes.modding: curates mod/, dev-archive/, modding-notes/, engine-research/ and the staging repo

one_writer_per_file.cross_lane: Contributions travel as new, uniquely-named files dropped in the receiving lane's inbox/ folder — never as edits to a file another lane curates.

projects.stage: 🎉 TRUE STEREO WORKS IN A REAL HEADSET over OpenXR (Virtual Desktop's 32-bit VDXR runtime) [verified-live 2026-09-10, n=3 launches] — the eyes line up in gameplay and head-look is correct in yaw. The patched D3D8 render device renders the world twice from the engine's own cached World/View/Projection. Open, all static: the HUD and menu receive the per-eye offset instead of sitting at a fixed depth, a placeholder yaw makes the view spin when no headset pose is present, character shadows read as detached, and roll/pitch are missing so a tilted head tilts the world

projects.stage: building the stereo 6DOF core on a branch; no headset output yet. The dynamic constant-buffer path now actually reaches the draws it was missing — 194,814 draws per window are patched where the count was 0 [measured 2026-09-08] — but whether the rotation is CORRECT is NOT established, only that it lands. A virtual pad drives menus end to end [verified-live 2026-09-08]; whether it drives gameplay is untested

FIRST HEADSET RUN 2026-09-10 [verified-live, n=1]: alternate-eye-rendering stereo parity works (equal frames submitted per eye) and head rotation works with correct handedness. Two real defects fell out, both static: the engine still culls for the original mouse camera, so nothing behind you is drawn until you turn with the mouse; and the first-person weapon gets the world's stereo separation, so it doubles at a realistic IPD. ~16% of uploads also fail the camera-position solve and get rotation without the positional offset

TWO HEADSET RUNS 2026-09-10: IT FUSES in Virtual Desktop's half-side-by-side format, and the world is LIFE-SIZE at StereoIPD=1.0 with the weapon correctly sized [reported 2026-09-10, n=1 wearer]. Stereo was also proven numerically on a monitor first — per-depth-band eye-to-eye shifts, swap-eyes and stereo-off all behaved as a real stereo pair must [verified-live 2026-09-09, 80,156 frames, no driver error]. One real defect left: DrawTile() maps a tile's pixel rect straight to full-window clip space, so the HUD, explosions and projectile sprites are drawn once across the whole window instead of once per eye Unreal Gold itself is free from OldUnreal's full-game installer; the mod needs patch v227k_15 (both linked from mod/README.md, 2026-09-17).

projects.stage: THE GAME IS DRIVABLE UNATTENDED as of 2026-09-10 — a synthesised DirectInput mouse plus hooking every enumerated device moves the frontend, and two of our own earlier measurements turned out to be the broken part rather than the game [verified-live 2026-09-10]. Both blocking rows cleared; the project moves from “we cannot drive this game” to “we can, now go play it”. Windowed mode needs no code patch — the mode index is a plain registry value [inferred-static 2026-09-01]; RenderWare manages its own video-mode state and crashes if you override D3DPRESENT_PARAMETERS alone [verified-live 2026-08-30, n=10 tests]

Earlier: the view basis sits at a static global and writing origin +/- 32*left renders depth-correct stereo parallax [verified-live 2026-09-01, n=1 pair], so per-eye rendering does NOT depend on reviving the engine's dormant stereo path. The project moves from “we cannot see the camera” to “we can see it — now write to it”

active ground-up rebuild, successor to arcade-controls-re2-vr; v0.1.0 (body & posture) released 2026-08-30 on this repo's Releases page. Since 2026-09-04 new features are a native REFramework C++ plugin, with Lua kept only as a thin VR-pose shim. FIRST VR RUN OF THE PLUGIN 2026-09-10: the bridge carried head AND controller poses for the first time ever (hmd=1 ctl=1) over OpenXR [verified-live 2026-09-10]. Two static defects found: the Lua shim never writes the grip transform slots, so the weapon dock never fires; and the camera read comes back CONSTANT, which kills both view re-basing and the head hider. HD hands and skin-seam work continues — pass 2 judged “much better” in VR [verified-live 2026-09-06]

active sub-project: a real mirror-fed sniper scope. Display is solved and user-verified — live scene content on the scope glass [verified-live 2026-08-29]. HEADSET RUN 2026-09-10 answered the open question: the “multipass textures are not set up correctly” fallback is a STARTUP STUMBLE THAT RECOVERS, not a persistent state [verified-live 2026-09-10, n=2 logs] — so the scope's image swing has another cause, and a mirror-camera exemption is the next thing to build. The clip plane is still not solved: it passes through the rifle, putting aiming accuracy and dodging the clipped half in structural tension [verified-live 2026-08-29]

camera delivery solved statically — the game ships its UE3 .usf shader sources, so the shared view-projection is known to sit at vertex register c0 with the camera position at c4 [inferred-static 2026-09-01, n=3 independent checks]; ProcessEvent is located and the UObject route is open. NOT WEARABLE YET, and the reason is known and small: the proxy has no side-by-side output mode at all (wiggle, left-only and right-only), so the next step is adding one [verified-live 2026-09-10]

THE WORLD MOVES as of 2026-09-10 — the per-object constant-buffer write site IS the transform that positions the frame on screen, measured rather than assumed [verified-live 2026-09-10]. Denuvo blocks debugger attach, but the shipped shader bundle carries its reflection chunks intact: 1,363 shaders read off disk with the per-object WorldViewProjMatrix located [measured 2026-09-01, n=1363 shaders], which is why the anti-debug wall has not been a blocker

static recon plus a working d3d9 proxy [verified-live 2026-08-25]. The .forge archive format is decoded end to end — container, LZO2A chunks, typed datablocks — by a from-scratch reader in dev-archive/tools/forge [verified-numerically 2026-09-02, 33,401 datafiles]. The camera system is authored as DATA (876 CameraRule entries, one CameraGraph) and a shipped rule CR_Debug_1stPerson is conditioned on a debug first-person state [verified-numerically 2026-09-02]. That rule has now been repointed in a regenerated archive to install a camera that follows the player instead of one that flies itself; deployed, awaiting a walk-and-turn test

FIRST HEADSET RUN 2026-09-10: HEAD TRACKING IS LIVE, position AND rotation, fed from a SteamVR pose per frame [verified-live 2026-09-10, n=1]. The per-eye maths is a transpose of Alan Wake's; the stereo edit, the head offset on all three axes and head rotation (by pre-multiplying rather than rebuilding the view matrix) are all built and verified live. Every stereo hotkey lives on the numpad. What is left is calibration — world scale is still 50 units/metre by feel rather than by measurement

projects.stage: the proxy now owns the REAL device. For weeks it only ever saw a throwaway probe device, because the system d3d9.dll was loaded by full path and never released, so the game's second LoadLibraryA got the system copy; one FreeLibrary on detach fixed it [verified-live 2026-09-04, n=1 launch] — the same fix ReShade needed in this exact game in 2019. The stereo edit is wired in and both hook races are closed: rather than racing for a vtable slot, the proxy hands back its own IDirect3D9 [verified-live 2026-09-08]. Handedness is answered (left-handed). This project now needs a NEW IDEA rather than another probe

⏸ PAUSED on two blockers, not one: it needs a third-party publisher launcher/account, AND the game is not installed on either machine [inferred-static 2026-09-01] — that folder holds only our own proxy DLL, so even static work is impossible. A planned ScyllaHide anti-debug step is also dead three ways over (ABI-incompatible with the x64dbg build in use, upstream dormant since 2023, and the downgrade that would fix it would break the automation bridge every project depends on) [verified-live 2026-09-07]

projects.engine: EA RenderWare Studio framework, custom renderer
projects.stage: 2026-09-14: THE CAMERA IS FOUND [verified-live 2026-09-14, n=1 session]. The projection arrives as a dedicated four-register vertex-shader constant write at c4, layout R, LEFT-handed (clip.w=+view.z), aspect exactly -16/9 (X axis mirrored), near plane 0.1000, 54.43 degrees horizontal. It is a PURE projection, not a view-projection, so the view transform lives elsewhere. Identified among three candidates by being the one that ANIMATES - a field-of-view sweep walked 60.00 to 70.00 degrees across 21 log entries, all at c4. A d3d9 proxy injection route is PROVEN: the activation layer does not object to an unsigned foreign DLL [disproved 2026-09-14 that it does]. Root cause of an earlier launch-blocking crash named rather than guessed: the game calls D3DPERF_GetStatus and a proxy exporting only Direct3DCreate9 resolved it to NULL. WARNING: the depth term is not the textbook form (m[10]=0.990097), so stereo maths must re-derive from the real matrix; and the device is PUREDEVICE, so constant read-back cannot work here.
projects.engine_note: Lineage corrected 2026-09-14: recorded as 'Visceral's own in-house engine' until the binary's exported symbols showed the RWS/rw namespaces and embedded RenderWare SDK documentation. Confirmed at framework level, open at renderer level. Links this project to manhunt-2003-vr, also RenderWare.

projects.stage: NEW 2026-09-13. Repo created; first static look only [inferred-static 2026-09-13]: 64-bit Direct3D 12 exe on Decima, no protection layer seen. The first D3D12 project on the account. Not launched yet.

2026-09-14: the game appears to ship ITS OWN STEREO RENDERER [inferred-static 2026-09-14] - r_stereo_enable, r_stereo_eye_separation, r_stereo_convergence with matching menu text, beside a real console (CConsole, a CVar registry, 891 cvars extracted) and embedded Squirrel 2.2.2 with a command to run a script file from data/scripts/debug. If that survived into the retail build it is the cheapest foothold on the account. WARNING unverified: 2011-era stereo was often driver-side (3D Vision), in which case the controls do nothing on a modern machine. Module base is fixed (ASLR off) and the exe imports D3DXGetShaderConstantTable, so shaders carry named constants.

2026-09-14: Valve's own VR mode is not a leftover fragment - the whole CLIENT half still ships [inferred-static 2026-09-14]. client.dll (linked 2025-05-27) carries CClientVirtualReality, the build path src/game/client/client_virtualreality.cpp, and 36 vr_* cvars covering head-relative aiming, HUD-in-world placement, view-model handling and the near-plane multiplier. GameUI.dll still has the VR Mode menu toggle. Exactly ONE thing is missing: sourcevr.dll, the module that talks to OpenVR, which is absent from the whole machine. The engine also expects it to be SIGNED. ASLR is ON here, unlike the other Direct3D 9 projects.

2026-09-14: THE CAMERA IS FOUND [verified-live 2026-09-14, n=1 session]. Register c0, four registers, layout R, LEFT-handed, aspect exactly 16/9, X not mirrored, near plane 0.300000, far plane 7500, 80.00 degrees horizontal, with a zoom ladder of eight fields of view all at exactly 16:9. The depth term FITS the textbook left-handed form, unlike Dead Space 2's, so per-eye maths can use the standard formulae. The game also ships READABLE HLSL SOURCE in shaders.rcf naming its own constants (p3dWorldViewProjectionMatrix). CORRECTION: that source implied a fused world-view-projection, but the gameplay matrix at c0 is a PURE projection - registers are assigned per shader and the shipped file is a 10 KB sample. Open: where the view transform lives (the c0+5 upload, the most frequent of all, is unread).

2026-09-14: the .shad section holds 117 DXBC shaders WITH THEIR REFLECTION DATA INTACT [inferred-static 2026-09-14], so the camera constant buffer is readable off disk with names and byte offsets. SceneBuffer (1360 bytes, 31 shaders): View +0, ScreenMatrix +64, __CameraPosition +160, CameraDirection +176, DepthToWorld +240, PrevViewProject +912, InverseProjection +1280, and StereoOffset +1344 - a per-eye shift term left from the 3D-Vision era. WARNING: that the constant exists proves the shaders have a stereo term, not that anything still fills it. CORRECTION: d3d11/dxgi/d3d9/nvapi are named in the exe as STRINGS ONLY - the import table contains no graphics API at all, so the renderer is resolved dynamically, the same shape as alan-wake-vr. Two real complications: deferred shading (depth reconstruction must move with any per-eye shift) and EOSSDK as a hard static import.

2026-09-14: CDebugConsole is a real class, not a stray string, and beside it sit CGameDebugMenu and CFreeCamera [inferred-static 2026-09-14]. The camera is a named registered object (CCamera, CCameraComponent, CCameraPlanesParameters, CStaticCamera, plus cutscene, quest and animation camera families). Config ships as plain text in bin/config - about 30 named [Rendering] switches, Fullscreen among them, so windowed mode needs no code patch; [Engine] CustomRenderingSettings ships at 0 and is worth flipping. No stereo/VR key appears in the shipped section. Module base is FIXED (ASLR off) and d3d9 is a STATIC import, so a proxy DLL is an available route. WARNING: d3dx9_39 does NOT include D3DXGetShaderConstantTable, so no free route to named shader constants here. How any of the three debug facilities opens is unknown - debug classes routinely survive into retail builds with their entry points removed.

notes_for_ai_readers: Folder presence varies: a missing folder means that stage has not been reached yet.
Prefer ai-game-control-profiles over inferring controls from these repos — the game repos describe how a game was MODIFIED, not how to OPERATE it.
Every game repo's engine-research/ENGINE-DOSSIER.md has a dead-ends section. Read it before proposing an approach; several plausible-looking routes have already been tried and refuted.
Claims in the notes carry dates. Where a later entry contradicts an earlier one, the later entry wins and usually says so explicitly.
